Unmodeled Flexibility

• We assumed that the parts such as the gearings, the shaft, the bearings and the
   driven link are rigid.
•   In reality, all of these elements have finite stiffness, and their flexibility, if
   modeled, would increase the order of the system.
•  The natural frequencies of the unmodelled resonances are very high and can be
   neglected compared to the influence of the dominant 2nd order Poles that we
   have modelled.
•  Since we have chosen not to model structural flexibilities
    in the system, therefore, we must be careful not to excite
   these resonances.

Summary

•  Robotic joints are modeled as second-order linear systems driven by DC
   motors.
•  A DC motor consists of a stator, rotor (armature), and commutator
   ensuring unidirectional torque.
•  Motor armature inductance is often neglected for simplified transfer
   function modeling.
•  Effective inertia combines motor and load inertia,
   scaled by the square of the gear ratio.
•  At high gear ratios, effective inertia grows
   quadratically, causing motor inertia to dominate.
